questions.q: Consider a parallel plate capacitor which is maintained at potential $200 \mathrm{~V}$. The separation distance between the plates of capacitor and the area of plates are $1 \mathrm{~mm}$ and $20 \mathrm{~cm}^2$, respectively. Calculate displacement current in $1 \mu \mathrm{s}$.
questions.solution: Displacement current, $\begin{aligned} I_d & =\varepsilon_0 \frac{d \phi}{d t}=\varepsilon_0 \frac{\Delta \phi}{\Delta t} \\ & =\varepsilon_0 \frac{\Delta E A}{\Delta t} \quad(\because \phi=E \cdot A)\end{aligned}=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \cdot \Delta V \cdot A}{\Delta t \cdot d} \quad \left(\because$E=$\frac{V}{d}\right) Here, \Delta$V=200 $\mathrm{~V}, \begin{aligned}\Delta$t & =1 \mu $\mathrm{s}=$10^{-6} $\mathrm{~s},$\\ d & =1 $\mathrm{~mm}=$1 $\times$10^{-3} $\mathrm{~m}$\\ $\text { and } \quad$A & =20 $\mathrm{~cm}^2=20 $\times$10^{-4} $\mathrm{~m}^2\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quadI_d \text{ and } =\frac{8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 200 \times 20 \times 10^{-4}}{10^{-6} \times 10^{-3}}\\ \text{ and } =3.5 $\times$10^{-3} $\mathrm{~A}=$3.5 \mathrm{~mA}\end{aligned}

questions.q: Electromagnetic waves travel in a medium with a speed of $\text{2} \times {\text{10}}^{8} \text{m}s^{- 1} .$ The relative permeability of the medium is $1$. Find the relative permittivity.
questions.solution:
Here, $\text{v} = 2 \times {10}^{8} \text{m}s^{- 1}$ and ${μ}_{r} = 1$

The speed of electromagnetic waves in a medium is given by

$\text{v} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\text{\mu} \text{ε}}} \text{,} \text{....(i)}$

where $\mu$ and $ε$ are absolute permeability and absolute permittivity of the medium.

Now, $\mu = {μ}_{0} {μ}_{r}$ and $ε = {ε}_{0} {ε}_{r}$

Therefore, the equation (i) becomes

$\text{v} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{μ}_{0} {μ}_{r} \times {ε}_{0} {ε}_{r}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{μ}_{0} {ε}_{0}}} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{μ}_{r} {ε}_{r}}} = \dfrac{\text{c}}{\sqrt{{μ}_{r} {ε}_{r}}}$

$\text{or} {ε}_{r} = \dfrac{c^{2}}{v^{2} {μ}_{r}} = \dfrac{{\left(3 \times {10}^{8}\right)}^{2}}{{\left(2 \times {10}^{8}\right)}^{2} \times 1} = \text{2.25}$

questions.q: Calculate the wavelength of the $k_a$ line for $z=31$, when $a=5 \times 10^7 \mathrm{~Hz}^{1 / 2}$ for a characteristic X-ray spectrum.
questions.solution:
Given, $z=31$ and $a=5 \times 10^7 \mathrm{~Hz}^{1 / 2}\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{v} & =a(z-1) \\
\text { or } \quad v & =a^2(z-1)^2 \\
& =\left(5 \times 10^7\right)^2(31-1)^2 \\
& =25 \times 10^{14} \times 30 \times 30 \\
& =2.25 \times 10^{18} \mathrm{~Hz} \\
\therefore \quad & =\frac{c}{\lambda} \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{c}{v} \\
& =\frac{3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}}{2.25 \times 10^{18} \mathrm{~Hz}} \\
& =1.33 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~m} \\
& =1.33 Å
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A conducting ring of radius $1m$ is placed in a uniform magnetic field~$B$,~of $0 . 01tesla$ oscillating with frequency $100$ Hz with its plane at right angles to $\overset{→}{B}$. What will be the induced electric field?
questions.solution:
In a constant magnetic field, conducting ring oscillates with a frequency of $100$ Hz.

i.e.,~$\text{T} = \dfrac{1}{100}\text{s}$,~in time $\dfrac{\text{T}}{2}$

~

to zero.

$⇒$~Induced emf $= \dfrac{\text{change in flux}}{\text{time}}$

$= \dfrac{BA}{T / 2} = \dfrac{2BA}{T} = \dfrac{2B \times \pir^{2}}{T} = \dfrac{2 \times 0 .01 \times \pi \times {1}^{2}}{1 / 100} = 4\pivolts$

The induced electric field along the circle, using Maxwell equation, is,$∮ \overset{→}{E} \cdot d\overset{→}{l} = - \dfrac{dϕ}{dt} = A\dfrac{dB}{dt} = e$

$⇒ E = \dfrac{1}{2\pir} \times \left(\pir^{2} \times \dfrac{\text{d}B}{\text{d}t}\right) = \dfrac{e}{2\pir} = \dfrac{4\pi}{2\pir} = 2Vm^{- 1}$

questions.q:
The energies required to set up in a cube of side $10$ cm,~$( a )$ A uniform electric field of ${10}^{7}Vm^{- 1}$ and~$( b )$~A~uniform magnetic field if $0 . 25Wbm^{- 2}$, are respectively about
\left({μ}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}Hm^{- 1}, {ϵ}_{0} = 8 . 9 \times {10}^{- 12}Fm^{- 1}\right)$
questions.solution:
Recall the formula of energy in terms of electric field and magnetic field strength,

${E}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}\left(E\right)2V \text{ and } {E}_{B} = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}\left(Bc\right)2V ⇒ {E}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}\left(E\right)2V ⇒ {E}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 8 . 9 \times {10}^{- 12} \times \left({10}^{7}\right)2 \times {10}^{- 3} = 0 . 445J ⇒ {E}_{B} = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}\left(Bc\right)2V ⇒ {E}_{B} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 8 . 9 \times {10}^{- 12} \times \left(0 . 25\right)2 \times \left(3 \times {10}^{8}\right)2 \times {10}^{- 3} = 25J$
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.q: The electric field for an electromangetic wave in free space is $\mathbf{E}=\mathbf{i} 30 \cos  \left(k z-5 \times 10^8 t\right)$, where magnitude of $E$ is in $\mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m}$. The magnitude of wave vector, $k$ is (velocity of em wave in free space $=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} )$
questions.solution:
The given
$\mathbf{E}=\mathbf{i} 30 \cos \left(k z-5 \times10^8 t\right)$
We know that,
$\mathbf{E}= \mathrm{iV} \cos (k z-\omegat)$
Comparing the both equations,
$\omega=5 \times10^8 $\mathrm{rad}$/ \mathrm{s}$
But we know that also
K=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda} \text { and } \omega=$2 \pi \nu$
where, $\lambda$ is wavelength and $v$ is frequency of the wave
\begin{array}{ll}$
\therefore & $\frac{\omega}{k}=\frac{2 \pi v}{2 \pi / \lambda}=$v \lambda=C \\
\Rightarrow & $C=\frac{\omega}{k}$\\
\text {or }& $k=\frac{\omega}{C}=\frac{5 \times 10^8}{3 \times 10^8}$\\
\Rightarrow & $k=\frac{5}{3}=$1.66 $\mathrm{rad}$/ $\mathrm{m}$
\end{array}$
